candidate.answerReason: The two legs have lengths 4 and 11, so the total distance is 15 units.

methods.label: Add the two travel distances
methods.explanation:
Add the lengths of both parts of the journey. Each length is the absolute value of the change in position, so the total distance is
\[
|-6-(-2)|+|5-(-6)|
=4+11=\boxed{15}
\]
units. The answer is choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
methods.levelReason: Only number-line distances, subtraction of signed integers, and addition of the two nonnegative lengths are needed.

candidate.annotationRationale: The mathematical target is interpreting travel distance as nonnegative lengths on a number line. Signed subtraction and absolute-value evaluation support the two calculations. The broader mixed-operation criteria of cnm_013 are unnecessary for this short solution.
